can_do_statement: Can use a non-defining relative clause with 'which' as the object.
example_raw:
The best of all was a marble statue which my aunt gave me. (Bangladesh; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Bengali; Pass)

Thanks for your letter which I received a few days ago. (Greece; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Linking secondary descriptive information to a main noun
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a non-defining relative clause with 'which' to add extra, non-essential information
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance from core clause by adding optional descriptive layer

positives: The best of all was a marble statue, which my aunt gave me.
I liked the book, which I received a few days ago.
negatives: The best of all was a marble statue, which sat on the table.
This is the car which I bought.

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses, 'the person who/that, the thing that, the (only) one who/that' as a focusing device.
example_raw:
The thing that was great is that the weather was really warm and it didn't rain. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; French; Pass)

The thing that I love most is going to the shops. (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

The person who sat next to me was her. (Vietnam; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)

The person who called me was my best friend. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Catalan; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Focusing attention on a specific entity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'the thing that' or 'the person who' to emphasize a particular subject
ontology.agency_or_distance: Agency in structuring information for emphasis

positives: The thing that was great is the weather.
The person who sat next to me was her.
negatives: A person who does that is bad.
The thing was that it rained.

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses with 'where' to define nouns referring to place.
example_raw:
The city where I live is very nice and extremely charming. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; ; Pass)

But if they are going to a place where you go every year you should go with your friends, you will have more fun. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

We went to the area where I used to live when I was a child near the Highlands. (Czech Republic; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Czech; Pass)>

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'where' after a place noun to define which place is meant
ontology.agency_or_distance: Spatial anchoring of an event to a specific location

positives: The city where I live is nice.
We went to the area where I used to live.
negatives: I know where you live.
This is where we met.

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses with 'when' to define nouns relating to time.
example_raw:
The day when he had to go back to Korea, I could not stop myself crying. (Korea, South; B1 THRESHOLD; 1999; Korean; Pass)

I really remember the day when I lost my suitcase in the airport. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I was in the class at the time when they made the movie, so you will be able to see me on TV. (Poland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Polish; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'when' after a time noun to define exactly which time is being discussed
ontology.agency_or_distance: Temporal anchoring of an event to a specific time reference

positives: I remember the day when he went back.
I was there at the time when they made it.
negatives: I know when he arrived.
When I saw him, he was sad.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-defining relative clause with 'who' as the object.
example_raw:
What I liked most was the friend I made there, a green-eyed chubby boy, who I played with till dinner time, when I had to go home. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Portuguese; Pass)

She turned around and, she couldn't believe it, it was an old classmate Tom, who she hadn't seen for ages! (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Adding non-essential information about a person
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using non-defining relative clauses with 'who' as the object to add extra details
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance from core identifying features by adding supplementary description

positives: It was Tom, who she hadn't seen for ages.
My brother, who I love, is nice.
negatives: My brother, who lives here, is nice.
The man who I saw was tall.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause, without a relative pronoun.
example_raw:
My friends said the clothes I wore were very old, and they didn't like them. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

All my friends gave me a present but the one I liked best was John's. (Portugal; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Portuguese; Pass)

Here I have the information you want. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Spanish - European; Pass)

[talking about video calls] You can see the person you are calling LIVE!!! (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Greek; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Defining a noun implicitly by attaching a subject and verb directly
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Dropping the relative pronoun in defining clauses when it is the object
ontology.agency_or_distance: Efficiency in communication by omitting redundant syntactic markers

positives: The clothes I wore were old.
Here is the information you want.
negatives: I know that you want it.
She said that I am wrong.

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses and non-defining relative clauses ending in a preposition, with 'who/which/that' as the complement of the preposition.
example_raw:
Thank you very much for having provided us with valuable information about your finance services, which we are greatly interested in. (China; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Chinese; Pass)

I would like to do some painting, which I am quite good at. (Switzerland; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; French; Pass)

They have three wonderful children who I love to play with. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1998; Swedish; Pass)

He was involved in a case that he had nothing to do with! (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Connecting a relative pronoun to its required preposition
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Ending a relative clause with a preposition when the pronoun is the complement
ontology.agency_or_distance: Syntactic deferral by moving the preposition to the end of the clause

positives: They have three children who I love to play with.
It was a case that he had nothing to do with!
negatives: I know the man who is with her.
The book which is on the table is mine.

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses with 'why' after 'reason', to give an explanation and for focus.
example_raw:
The reason why I love it is that it's quite original because it's about a woman who can see ghosts. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Spanish - European; Pass)

This is the reason why we are changing our working hours. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; German; Pass)

This is the main reason why it is so famous and popular as well. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; French; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'the reason why' to focus on the cause of a situation
ontology.agency_or_distance: Asserting the causal link as the focal point of the sentence

positives: The reason why I love it is this.
This is the reason why we are changing it.
negatives: I don't know why he did it.
There is no reason to do that.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'who' or 'that' as the object.
example_raw:
My friends are the people who I love most. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

They filmed two actors who I don't really know arguing and kissing after it. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Catalan; Pass)

It was Sarah, a girl who I met in Spain on my holiday last year. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Swiss German; Pass) 

We are going with my friends Paolo and Ontorio, the guys who you met yesterday. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Italian; Pass)

So I sent a letter to the school and they have sent me the details of the people that I'm going to stay with. (Japan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Japanese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Defining a person by the actions of another subject
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'who' or 'that' as the object of a defining relative clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: Specifying identity based on interaction with a distinct subject

positives: My friends are the people who I love most.
It was Sarah, a girl who I met in Spain.
negatives: My brother, who I love, is tall.
The man who is standing there is my dad.

can_do_statement: Can use defining and non-defining relative clauses with 'whose name'.
example_raw:
We have a new employee whose name is Mary Watts. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Spanish - European; Pass)

It was a very famous football player, whose name was known all over the world. (Russia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Russian; Pass)

I have many friends but I'll tell you about my best friend, whose name is Nicos. (Greece; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Greek; Pass)

He has got a friend whose name is Robert. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; German; Pass

The man whose name I can't remember, wrote a serious looking message. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Swiss German; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Linking an entity to its specific identifying label
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'whose name' to provide the exact name of a person or thing
ontology.agency_or_distance: Direct nominal identification attached to a reference

positives: We have a new employee whose name is Mary.
He has a friend whose name is Robert.
negatives: I don't know whose book this is.
Whose name was called?

can_do_statement: Can use non-defining relative clauses with 'whose', to give additional information.
example_raw:
And I was initially employed to be an entrance assistant, whose job was to keep the queue under control as well as keeping the area clean. (China; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Chinese; Pass)

I was at the concert when I met a friend of mine whose job is to organise shows like that. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Italian; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a non-defining relative clause with 'whose' to add extra details about what someone owns or their relationships
ontology.agency_or_distance: Distance from core identity by adding supplementary possessive description

positives: I met a friend, whose job is to organise shows.
I have an assistant, whose parents are nice.
negatives: The man whose car was stolen was sad.
I wonder whose this is.

can_do_statement: Can use defining relative clauses with 'whose', to give more information about relationship.
example_raw:
I visited several primary schools in Canberra and had opportunities to teach not only Australian children but also Vietnamese children whose parents immigrated to Australia. (Japan; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Japanese; Pass)

Mary is a young lady whose parents had died and she had nobody else but an aunt to live with. (Brazil; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Defining a person by their relationships or possessions
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'whose' in a defining relative clause to specify exactly who is being discussed based on relation
ontology.agency_or_distance: Anchoring identity to an external, possessed relational entity

positives: I teach children whose parents immigrated here.
Mary is a lady whose parents died.
negatives: My friend, whose job is great, is rich.
I wonder whose coat this is.

can_do_statement: Can use a relative clause to refer to a whole clause or sentence, often to express an opinion or evaluation or give a reason.
example_raw:
It is now possible to send a letter and receive an answer within ten minutes, which is a good thing if you want to buy a house, a car etc. (Denmark; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Danish; Pass)

In addition, zoological gardens allow us to get to know the lifestyles of some animals better, which is very important from the point of view of their protection. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Polish; Pass)

I have also visited the dance shows and the art exhibitions, as well as the talks by writers, which were all really brilliant. (Switzerland; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; French; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which' referring back to a whole clause to give an opinion or evaluation
ontology.agency_or_distance: Metalinguistic distance in commenting on a complete thought

positives: He passed the exam, which is great.
It was raining, which meant we stayed inside.
negatives: The book, which I read, is mine.
I bought a car which is very fast.

can_do_statement: Can use a finite subordinate clause with conjunctions ('even though, (al)though, while if') to introduce contrast, before or after a main clause.
example_raw:
You should come with your sister even though you would rather be alone. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; French; Pass)

Even though I am currently quite busy, I will be very glad to take part in the Conference dinner. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 1999; Italian; Pass)

Although he was famous, I didn't like him. (Chile; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

Though we are not studying at the same school now, we always keep in touch. (Vietnam; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)

The main actor is my favorite actor, although I can't remember his name. (Taiwan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Chinese; Pass)

I think going on holiday with your parents won't be very much fun, while if you go with your friends you will enjoy yourself much more. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'even though' or 'although' to introduce an unexpected contrast to the main clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: Navigating contradictory facts by explicitly marking contrast

positives: Although he was famous, I didn't like him.
Though we are not studying there, we keep in touch.
negatives: He is famous though.
I will see if he is there.

can_do_statement: Can use a finite subordinate clause with 'because', after a main clause, to introduce reasons.
example_raw:
I love her because she is friendly. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Bengali; Pass)

I like my television because it is big and modern. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Arabic - Other; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Explaining the cause of a state or action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'because' in the middle of a sentence to provide a reason for the main clause
ontology.agency_or_distance: Connecting an outcome directly to its originating cause

positives: I love her because she is friendly.
I like my television because it is big.
negatives: Because it was raining, we stayed inside.
Because of the rain, we left.
